notes.src/core/analytics/config.ts: Kept deliberately, both of them. `validateProviderConfig` is dead code that a *published page* describes: `core/guide/reference/logs.md` documents its two error messages and says in so many words that it 'is exported but never called anywhere in the SDK', generated from `src/docs/content/core-logs.notes.ts`. Deleting it — or even dropping the `export` keyword — makes that page wrong, and rewriting it is a `src/docs/**` change. `PROVIDER_SETTINGS` rides along: it is only reachable in-file now, but `validateProviderConfig`'s parameter type is `typeof PROVIDER_SETTINGS`, so unexporting it breaks declaration emit for the function above it. Retire the pair together with the doc rows, or not at all. (Wave 11 did delete this file's genuinely orphaned `ANALYTICS_EVENTS` and `getProviderConfig`, and unexported `DEFAULT_DEBUG_CONFIG`.)
notes.src/core/analytics/data-layer-manager.ts: `DataLayerManager`'s singleton `dataLayer` is imported widely; only the class name has no importer. The class name has no external importer, but its singleton instance in the same file does, and the class must stay exported for a different reason: `declaration: true` is on, so an exported `const x = X.getInstance()` cannot be emitted in the .d.ts if `X` itself is private to the module. Unexporting it turns a green type-check into a failing build. Nothing to fix — this is the shape a `.getInstance()` singleton has here.
